source.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
source.authors: Yun-Fei Xie; Howard H. Qian; Shi-Yi Lan; Kai-Yu Hang; Chen Wei

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends a PRH-inspired idea to robotics and reports sensorimotor-alignment results, but measures each model’s sensory-to-trajectory alignment rather than convergence between models’ representations.
record.gate_note: S2 compares sensory and motion neighborhoods within a robot dataset for each model, then relates that score to task success. This is a related but different construct from the claim versions’ cross-model representational convergence. The study does not measure pairwise convergence between independently trained models, convergence across scale, or shared features. Its findings are recorded under fits_no_version; none of the listed versions is directly tested. The paper also reports cited findings from other work; those are not rows.
record.test_reason: S2 applies PRH's CKNNA metric to compare one model's sensory embeddings with raw recorded end-effector trajectory geometry, not with another model's representation, then correlates that score with task success. The authors frame this as testing a PRH extension. Still, no pairwise convergence between independently trained models, seeds, or vision and language models is measured, and no mapping or shared-feature test is run. It is a related but different construct (model-to-data alignment as a capability proxy), so the findings go under fits_no_version. The reader's T3/discusses is replaced by T4: the study uses the PRH framing and metric as a tool and reports its own proxy's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim S2 correlates positively with task success across VLAs, raw VLMs, WAMs, and real-robot policies, and correlates more strongly than VQA or video-quality metrics. They claim it explains modality dominance, the frozen-encoder drop, cheap denoising skipping, and the importance of mid-depth blocks. They present this as extending PRH to robotics, while conceding the results are correlational with few models and a single real-robot setting.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and tests a sensorimotor nearest-neighbor alignment score, comparing one model’s sensory geometry with recorded trajectory geometry. It does not use the original claim’s cross-model representation-convergence comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The S2-success association varies with the reference embodiment (matched ALOHA r = +0.999 versus DROID r = +0.246 for three WAMs) and with the evaluated real-robot horizon (r = +0.831 at ℎ = 110 versus r = +0.429 at prespecified ℎ = 7). The paper reports positive associations across tested neighbor counts, implementation choices, and most tested horizons.

fits_no_version.finding: A model's sensory-to-trajectory neighborhood alignment (S2, a CKNNA variant) correlates with downstream task success across VLAs (r=+0.717), raw VLMs (r=+0.681), WAMs (r=+0.718), real-robot policies (r=+0.831 at an exploratory horizon; +0.429 at the prespecified h=7), and frozen encoders under BC/VRF. The correlation does not hold under task-reward RL or with an embodiment-mismatched reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment between an embodied model's sensory representation geometry and recorded motor-trajectory geometry tracks its task success, when the reference data match the robot's arm configuration and the policy relies on the representation.

fits_no_version.finding: S2 and its success correlation vary by feature modality, encoder freezing, denoising step, and block depth. Vision features carry the correlation in fine-tuned VLAs; text features do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within robot foundation models, sensorimotor alignment differs across feature sources and training choices in ways that track reported closed-loop phenomena.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned VLAs have higher mean S2 than raw VLMs at every feature position (Table 8: +12.7% to +45.0%). Within the 12 VLAs, the correlation also holds under architecture-group leave-one-out (Table 1: r +0.526 to +0.785).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robot fine-tuning increases a model's alignment with motor-trajectory geometry.

record.problems: The authors state that the evidence is correlational, model families and benchmarks are limited, some comparisons contain few models, and there is a single real-robot evaluation setting. The real-robot association is reported at an exploratory horizon and is weaker at the prespecified horizon. Several comparisons have only three models.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix includes exhaustive per-model S2 values across horizons and feature positions (Tables 2–4 and 9–10) and per-model WAM schedule values (Table 11). Those entries are not separately extracted because they are within-model sensory-to-trajectory measurements and do not test any listed cross-model convergence version; the relevant aggregate or explicitly discussed outcomes are represented above.

untested.parts: No cross-model representational comparison and no test that inter-model alignment rises with scale or capability. S2 rising with capability concerns alignment to trajectory data, not between models.
No vision-language model alignment on paired image-caption data.
No seed-to-seed comparison of same-architecture networks.
No linear map, stitching, relative representation, or unpaired matching between models.
No cross-model test of shared interpretable features or circuits.
The k, horizon, and reference-dataset sweeps vary S2's relationship with success, not a cross-model convergence measure.
No test of plateauing cross-model alignment or of shared data or objectives as its cause.

record.verdict_notes: The motor 'representation' is raw recorded trajectories, not a learned model, so the result does not bear on convergence between models. Not recorded as rows, and not needed for any version: Table 1 leave-one-out, the CogACT within-family r=+0.826 (p=0.191), Table 7 feature-position correlations, Table 8 group means, and the Table 6 DTW ablation. The real-robot r=+0.831 uses an exploratory horizon.

versions.untested_parts: No pairwise representation comparison between independently trained models, nor a test that cross-model alignment rises with model size or capability.
No measurement of alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions as both models improve.
No comparison of representations across random seeds of the same architecture.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test between models.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study varies S2 settings and reference datasets, but does not test whether cross-model convergence depends on similarity measures, neighbor settings, or input distribution.
No test of whether cross-model convergence plateaus or is explained by shared training data or objectives.
